29	mask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)
30	rmsn_b(dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
31	    r = SQRT (epsilon + (x DOT x) / |x|); y = x / r
32	    (dy - y ((y DOT dy) / |y|)) / r
33	  end
34	sm_b(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = p × (dy - (p DOT dy))
35	
36	(* ------------------------------- tactic 2/8: one vector, nine views ------ *)
37	matName(i: ZZ32): String =
38	    if i = 0 then "wte" elif i = 1 then "wpe" elif i = 2 then "lm_head" elif i = 3 then "attn_wq" elif i = 4 then "attn_wk"
39	    elif i = 5 then "attn_wv" elif i = 6 then "attn_wo" elif i = 7 then "mlp_fc1" else "mlp_fc2" end
40	matShape(i: ZZ32): (ZZ32, ZZ32) =
41	    if (i = 0) OR (i = 2) then (vocabSize, nEmbd) elif i = 7 then (4 nEmbd, nEmbd) elif i = 8 then (nEmbd, 4 nEmbd) else (nEmbd, nEmbd) end
42	matCount(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do (r, c) = matShape(i); r c end
43	matOffset(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#i] matCount(j)
44	nParams(): ZZ32 = matOffset(9)
45	view(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do (r, c) = matShape(i); view(p, matOffset(i), r, c) end
46	
47	(* -------------------- tactic 3/5: the corpus as one padded integer matrix - *)
48	corpus: Corpus = loadCorpus(corpusPath, blockSize, bosId)
49	
50	(* ------------------------- the step: keys -> (loss, flat gradient). Pure. -- *)
51	step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
52	    ids = corpus.tokens(b, 0); tg = corpus.tokens(b, 1); vm = corpus.valid(b); nv = SUM vm; pos = corpus.positions(b)
53	    (wte, wpe, lm, wq, wk, wv, wo, f1, f2) = (view(p, 0), view(p, 1), view(p, 2), view(p, 3), view(p, 4), view(p, 5), view(p, 6), view(p, 7), view(p, 8))
54	    h(m: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = heads(m, blockSize, nHead, headDim)
55	    u(t: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = unheads(t, nHead)
56	    (* -- forward, all (doc, pos) rows at once -- *)
57	    x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos); xp = rows(rmsn, x); x1 = rows(rmsn, xp)
58	    (q, k, v) = (x1 wq^T, x1 wk^T, x1 wv^T); (qh, kh, vh) = (h(q), h(k), h(v))
59	    a = rows(sm, mask + (qh kh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)); hc = u(a vh)
60	    x2 = xp + hc wo^T; x3 = rows(rmsn, x2); m0 = x3 f1^T; mr = 0.0 MAX m0; x4 = x2 + mr f2^T
61	    pr = rows(sm, x4 lm^T); loss = -(vm DOT log(pick(pr, tg))) / nv
62	    (* -- backward, one line under each forward line, bottom-up -- *)
63	    dL = diag(vm / nv) (pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize)); gLM = dL^T x4; dX4 = dL lm
64	    gF2 = dX4^T mr; dM0 = (dX4 f2) × (m0 > 0.0); gF1 = dM0^T x3; dX3 = dM0 f1
65	    dX2 = dX4 + rows(rmsn_b, dX3, x2); gWO = dX2^T hc; dh = h(dX2 wo)
66	    dVh = a^T dh; dS = rows(sm_b, a, dh vh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)
67	    dQh = dS kh; dKh = dS^T qh; (dQ, dK, dV) = (u(dQh), u(dKh), u(dVh))
68	    (gWQ, gWK, gWV) = (dQ^T x1, dK^T x1, dV^T x1); dX1 = dQ wq + dK wk + dV wv
69	    dXp = dX2 + rows(rmsn_b, dX1, xp); dX = rows(rmsn_b, dXp, x)
70	    gWTE = transpose(onehot(ids, vocabSize)) dX; gWPE = transpose(onehot(pos, blockSize)) dX
71	    (loss, flat(gWTE, gWPE, gLM, gWQ, gWK, gWV, gWO, gF1, gF2))
72	  end
73	
74	(* --------------------- Adam: three whole-vector expressions over p, m, v -- *)
75	adam(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], g: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], t: ZZ32, lr: RR64):
76	    (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
77	    m' = beta1 m + (1 - beta1) g
78	    v' = beta2 v + (1 - beta2) (g × g)
79	    p' = p - (lr (m' / (1 - beta1^t))) / (SQRT (v' / (1 - beta2^t)) + epsilon_A)
80	    (p', m', v')
81	  end
82	learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)
83	
84	(* --------------------------------------------------- training ----------- *)
85	run(): () = do
86	    println "microgpt flat | params " nParams() " | corpus " corpus.size() " x " (blockSize + 1) " | batch 1, 5 steps"
87	    bsz = 1
88	    p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := loadParams(weightsDir, matName, 9, nParams())
89	    m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
90	    v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
91	    for s <- seq(0#5) do
92	        t0 = nanoTime()
93	        (l, g) = step(p, keys(bsz, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => (s bsz + i) MOD corpus.size()))
94	        (p, m, v) := adam(p, m, v, g, s + 1, learningRate(s))
95	        println "step " (s + 1) " loss " l "  (" ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms)"
96	    end
97	  end
98	end

(* FlatArrays -- the array vocabulary of Run C4: what the shipped
   Vector/Matrix algebra lacks, declared once in the library's own style over
   the library's own arrays.  Round two's vocabulary (explorations/run-c/src)
   less the block, ravel, vector-gather and validity pieces that the corpus
   object of FlatData makes unnecessary; the inventory it was built against
   is round three's survey (explorations/run-c3/survey.md).  Views take their
   shapes at run time through the library's own reflect idiom
   (FortressLibrary.fss:1922-1934). *)
component FlatArrays
export FlatArrays
import NatReflect.{...}

(* ------------------------------------------------------- constructors ---- *)
vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).tabulate(f)
zeros(n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(0.0)
keys(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] = array[\ZZ32\](n).tabulate(f)
mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).tabulate(f)

(* ------------------------------------------- the elementwise algebra ----- *)
(* One declaration per operator, generic in the index type I, so a vector
   (I = ZZ32), a matrix ((ZZ32,ZZ32)) and a rank-3 array share it.  A scalar
   times an array is the library's juxtaposition and is not redeclared;
   + and - between two arrays of one shape, and + - MIN MAX between an array
   and a scalar, are the library's. *)
opr ×[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e b[i])
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e / b[i])
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e / s)
(* a comparison on an array is a 0/1 array *)
opr >[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => if e > s then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
opr SQRT[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => SQRT e)
exp[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => exp(e))
log[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => log(e))
(* diag(v) m scales the rows of m: the Dyalog's v ×⍤0 1 m.  A diagonal is a
   read-only Matrix view; the library's product forwards to its mul, which
   scales the rows without forming the matrix. *)
object Diag[\nat s\](d: Vector[\RR64,s\]) extends Matrix[\RR64,s,s\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; if i = j then d[i] else 0.0 end end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = fail("a diagonal is read-only")
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = fail("a diagonal is read-only")
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,s,0,s\] = array2[\U,s,s\]()
    mul[\nat s2\](other: Matrix[\RR64,s,s2\]): Matrix[\RR64,s,s2\] =
        other.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), e: RR64): RR64 => do (i, j) = ij; d[i] e end)
end
diag[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Diag[\s\] = Diag[\s\](v)

(* ----------------------------------------------------- transposes -------- *)
(* as functions: an API cannot declare a postfix operator (ledger row 133), so
   the model declares ^T itself over these; and a call result may not be
   followed by ^T at all (rows 144, 158) *)
transpose[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()
transpose[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\] = Transposed3[\a,b,c\](t)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------ views ----- *)
(* the (nr x nc) matrix at off in a flat vector, row-major *)
object PView[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](base: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(off + i c + j) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(off + i c + j, x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(off + i c + j, x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end

93	heads[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do

100	    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
101	    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
102	    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,cc\] = array2[\U,r,cc\]()
103	end

105	    UnheadsView[\a,b,c,r,cc\](base, nh)
106	unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do

110	(* a plane of a rank-3 array as a matrix, and every plane transposed *)
111	object PlaneView[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,b,c\]
112	    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get((p, i, j)) end
113	    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put((p, i, j), x) end
114	    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0((p, i, j), x) end

118	object Transposed3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]) extends Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\]
119	    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.get((p, j, i)) end
120	    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.put((p, j, i), x) end

126	(* +.×⍤2 : the library product on every pair of planes *)
127	opr juxtaposition[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
128	    (np, n, d) = x.sizes
129	    (yp, yn, yd) = y.sizes
130	    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, yd)
131	    for p <- 0#np do (plane(out, p)).assign((plane(x, p)) (plane(y, p))) end
132	    out
133	  end

135	opr +[\nat r, nat c, nat a, nat b, nat d\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,d\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
136	    t.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), e: RR64): RR64 => do (p, i, j) = ix; m[i,j] + e end)
137

140	   rows of two matrices; over a rank-3 array the rows are those of every plane.
141	   A parallel for over the rows, each written through a row view. *)
142	rows[\nat r, nat c\](f: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] -> Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
143	    (n, d) = m.sizes
144	    out = array[\RR64\](n, d)

146	    out

155	    (np, n, d) = t.sizes
156	    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, d)

1	(* FlatData -- the loaders and the corpus for MicroGptFlat (Run C4).
2	   The weights are nine text files, one matrix row per line, read straight
3	   into one flat vector in layout order; the corpus is one padded integer
4	   matrix (documents x block+1) with a length per document (Hsu's tactics
5	   3 and 5). The float parser is here because the library's strToFloat
6	   mis-parses a sign and overflows on a 17-digit mantissa (ledger row 140)
7	   and String.split is not a tokenizer (row 141). *)
8	component FlatData
9	export FlatData
10	import FlatArrays.{...}
11	import File.{...}
12	
13	(* decimal digits, optional '.', optional e/E exponent; leading '-' or '¯' *)
14	parseFloat(s: String): RR64 = do
15	    neg = (s[0] = '-') OR (s[0] = '¯')
16	    m: RR64 := 0.0
17	    scale: ZZ32 := 0
18	    ex: ZZ32 := 0
19	    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end
20	    seenPoint: Boolean := false
21	    n = |s|
22	    while (i < n) AND: ((s[i] =/= 'e') AND (s[i] =/= 'E')) do
23	        c = s[i]
24	        if c = '.' then seenPoint := true
25	        else
26	            m := 10.0 m + (c.codePoint - '0'.codePoint)
27	            if seenPoint then scale += 1 end
28	        end
29	        i += 1
30	    end
31	    if i < n then
32	        eneg = (s[i+1] = '-') OR (s[i+1] = '¯')
33	        j = if eneg OR (s[i+1] = '+') then i + 2 else i + 1 end
34	        ex := strToInt(s[j # (n - j)])
35	        if eneg then ex := -ex end
36	    end
37	    e10 = ex - scale
38	    r = if e10 >= 0 then m (10.0^e10)
39	        elif e10 >= -22 then m / (10.0^(-e10))
40	        else (m / (10.0^22)) / (10.0^(-e10 - 22)) end
41	    if neg then -r else r end
42	  end
43	
44	(* the space-separated numbers of a line, into out[off..]; returns how many *)
45	parseRow[\nat s\](line: String, out: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
46	    n = |line|
47	    i: ZZ32 := 0
48	    k: ZZ32 := 0
49	    while i < n do
50	        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
51	        else
52	            j: ZZ32 := i
53	            while (j < n) AND: (line[j] =/= ' ') do j += 1 end
54	            out[off + k] := parseFloat(line[i # (j - i)])
55	            k += 1
56	            i := j
57	        end
58	    end
59	    k
60	  end
61	(* the numbers of a line as a vector (two scans: count, then fill) *)
62	numbersOf(line: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
63	    cnt = parseRow(line, zeros(|line|), 0)
64	    out = zeros(cnt)
65	    parseRow(line, out, 0)
66	    out
67	  end
68	(* the lines of a file, up to the first empty one *)
69	readLines(path: String): Array[\String,ZZ32\] = do
70	    f = FileReadStream(path)
71	    cnt: ZZ32 := 0
72	    line: String := f.readLine()
73	    while |line| > 0 do cnt += 1; line := f.readLine() end
74	    f.close()
75	    g = FileReadStream(path)
76	    out = array[\String\](cnt).fill("")
77	    for i <- seq(0#cnt) do out[i] := g.readLine() end
78	    g.close()
79	    out
80	  end
81	(* one number per line *)
82	readVector(path: String, n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
83	    f = FileReadStream(path)
84	    v = zeros(n)
85	    for i <- seq(0#n) do v[i] := parseFloat(f.readLine()) end
86	    f.close()
87	    v
88	  end
89	
90	(* the weights: files name(0) .. name(count-1) under dir, every line's numbers
91	   appended in order into one vector of `total` values -- the layout is the
92	   caller's table, the loader only concatenates *)
93	loadParams(dir: String, name: ZZ32 -> String, count: ZZ32, total: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
94	    p = zeros(total)
95	    off: ZZ32 := 0
96	    for i <- seq(0#count) do
97	        for line <- seq(readLines(dir "/" name(i) ".txt")) do off += parseRow(line, p, off) end
98	    end
99	    if off =/= total then fail("loaded " off " numbers, the layout has " total) end
100	    p
101	  end
102	
103	(* the corpus: one document per line, interned a..z; the token matrix has
104	   width block+1, BOS before and after each document and in every unused
105	   slot, and a length per document (its characters plus the leading BOS) *)
106	object Corpus(tokm: Array[\ZZ32,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], len: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\], blk: ZZ32)
107	    size(): ZZ32 = |len|
108	    length(d: ZZ32): ZZ32 = len[d]
109	    token(d: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): ZZ32 = tokm[d, j]
110	    (* the keys of a batch b of documents, one row per (document, position):
111	       the tokens at position + off, the positions, and the 0/1 validity mask *)
112	    tokens(b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\], off: ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] =
113	        keys(|b| blk, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => tokm[b[r DIV blk], (r MOD blk) + off])
114	    positions(b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] =
115	        keys(|b| blk, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blk)
116	    valid(b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
117	        vec(|b| blk, fn (r: ZZ32): RR64 => if (r MOD blk) < len[b[r DIV blk]] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
118	end
119	loadCorpus(path: String, blk: ZZ32, bos: ZZ32): Corpus = do
120	    names = readLines(path)
121	    tokm = array[\ZZ32\](|names|, blk + 1).fill(bos)
122	    for d <- seq(0#|names|), j <- seq(0#|names[d]|) do tokm[d, 1 + j] := names[d][j].codePoint - 'a'.codePoint end
123	    Corpus(tokm, keys(|names|, fn (d: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 1 + |names[d]|), blk)
124	  end
125	end

1	<!-- What is established about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as it stands now, grouped by area: each entry the fact, its source and its test. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `FACTS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. -->
2	
3	# Facts on record
4	
5	## Execution model
6	
7	- F-7 **Walk and the compiled path share the parser and the phases, and only the compiled path runs the static type checker.** Walk switches the checker off, and no switch turns it on. So walk checks no static types of expressions: an ill-typed expression shows only when it runs, as a failed dispatch or as another run-time error, such as F-239's refusal of an `if` on a value that is not a `Boolean`. At load, walk refuses some ill-formed declarations: the `fortress-repo` skill's `interpreter.md`, "What walk checks", lists them, with their evidence in F-29 (`comprises` clauses), F-142 (the Meet Rule for Functional Methods) and F-145 (uncovered abstract methods and `override`). The phases and where the two paths part: the skill's "How a program runs". Detail: `explorations/repo-internals.md`, "The two worlds".
8	- F-9 **`fortress typecheck` checks a program against the compiler's library, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so it is no oracle for walk programs.** `Shell.java` calls `useCompilerLibraries()` for the command (row 69). P-12 has walk run the checker on its own programs after the switch-over, and walk cannot do so as it stands: it runs with type checking and the Scala checker off, the Java checker is gone (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:228-229`), and it has no case for the `CoercionInvocation` nodes that the checker inserts, by reading (row 833).
9	- F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled runtime"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). In a hot compiled loop, escape analysis removes the temporary boxes, and one box per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration stays (F-301), as long as C2's inline depth reaches each box's constructor chain (F-302). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4; `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` section 4.
10	- F-12 **On the compiled path, the scalar `RR64` loop `bench1t` ran in 0.74 s in one session's measurement; the loop still pays for its generator, for boxing and for a transaction check at each use of its accumulator.** `bench1t` is `for i <- seq(1#20000000) do acc := acc 0.9999999 + 0.0000001 end` on a `var acc: RR64`, with both literals written in the loop. The time is the median of three loop-only runs at one thread (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, "The four timings"). Times taken in different sessions differ on this machine, so compare only times from one session. What the loop does, read in its bytecode (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 5): the `seq` loop becomes the compiler prelude's `countedseqloop`, which runs the iterations in order by a recursive split over boxed indices, with a closure call per element; each value is boxed (F-11); and the accumulator is a volatile cell whose read and write each first call `BaseTask.inATransaction`, as for every mutable local (F-40, what a size costs at run time, whose sized loop pays the same check). Within the boxing and the cell, the report counts four allocations per iteration, an interface call to the native wrapper and the casts, the part that unboxed doubles and `double[]` would attack. No share of the 0.74 s is measured.
11	- F-17 **The bytecode cache can come up empty after a library order that reports exit 0.** Running the same commands again, one at a time, made the jars. The cause is not known. Check the five jars before a compiled run (the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md`, "The library order"). Detail: `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` section 1.
12	- F-18 **On the compiled path, the class loader makes the class of a generic instantiation at its first use, by rewriting the template's bytecode with ASM, and the rewriting only renames, so it gives no instance a `double[]` field.** The class is `InstantiatingClassloader`; the `fortress-repo` skill's "The compiled runtime" gives the mechanism. A size is part of the made class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, the object `Box` at size 3 in the probe component `pNatMeth`. Inside the class, the size's descriptor is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). A field of the template's type `T`, `LT;`, becomes `LFRR64;` in `Box⟦FRR64⟧`, and `[D` is no class name, so stamping alone keeps every number boxed (F-11). The team's direction for unboxing builds on this class per instantiation (the plan in `compiler/optimization/Unbox.java`; the loader's empty "expando" stub, `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172`), but a loader that stamps an `RR64` instance with a `double[]` field, way A4 of array decision A (P-85), does not exist and is unmeasured. Walk instantiates generics in its own evaluator, not by classes. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1; `coordinator/array-design.md` section 2 (probe 1); `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 3, way A4.
13	- F-19 **By the specification, the iterations of a `for` loop, the elements of a tuple, and the arguments of a call or an operator may run in parallel, and a program must assume that they do.** A `for` loop is sequential only if every generator is, as `seq(g)` or `sequential(g)` makes it. An implementation may also run them one after another (`evaluation/parallelism.tex:88-90`), so a program cannot count on parallel runs either. For the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator, each path starts a task only where it judges it worth it: walk by `TupleTask.worthSpawning`, which also governs a call's arguments, and the code generator by `ParallelismAnalyzer`. Compiled, the arguments of a function call and of a dotted method call fork where the analyzer marked the argument tuple (`CodeGen.evalArg`; F-350), and the analyzer marks no call written in the compiler's prelude (row 982). A `for` loop over a range without `seq` runs by splitting the range into `do … also do … end` blocks. Under walk, every such block is a task, and walk's library splits a `ZZ32` range down to chunks of `grainSize`, 16, elements, each run by the sequential range's methods, and a range with a stride down to single elements (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:20`). Compiled, the first block runs in place, and each other block forks only where `BaseTask.forkIfProfitable` judges it worth it, as tuple elements do; the compiler prelude's `parloop` splits down to `FORTRESS_LOOP_CHUNK` elements, 1 by default. `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the pool of worker threads (the `fortress-repo` skill, "Parallelism and mutable state"). By grep, no program under `explorations/`, the model programs and the probes, writes `spawn`, which starts an explicit thread, or an `also do` block, so their parallelism comes only from loops, tuples and arguments. The revival's tests under `ProjectFortress/` write both. Source: `Specification/basic/expressions/for.tex:28-32`, `tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:58-59`, `evaluation/parallelism.tex:50-80`.
14	- F-20 **Sizes, the `nat` and `int` static parameters, are values at run time; they check shapes, and no optimization uses them (F-40, what a size costs at run time).** The compiled checker checks them (F-67), and a sized program loads and runs compiled (F-129).
